text:
Tommy Novak has quietly become one of Pittsburgh's better scorers: 14 points in 18 games on under 16 minutes a night, including two goals in the win over Los Angeles that ended a four-game skid. He was a third-round pick in 2015 who bounced through the minors, and he is now playing the best hockey of his career.

Some of the finishing will cool. He is shooting 21.9% on 32 shots, and his range says closer to 14%. The Penguins have also scored 4.6 more goals than their chances deserve with him on the ice. But his own chances are honest: 6.1 expected goals, at a rate well above last season's.

The underlying game backs him up. Evolving-Hockey had his team creating +0.24 expected goals per 60 with him out there last season, 96th percentile among forwards, and Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him exiting his zone with the puck 59% of the time. We project about 54 points. Fewer goals, same useful player.
headline: Novak is giving Pittsburgh real middle six goals
